cpu_isolation.hardware: same host, CPU only; CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty; no model loaded
cpu_isolation.worker_protocol: Same recorded dataset, transformations, seed and rank-0 sampler; micro batch 8, one spawn worker. Stop after about 75 s at a 10-batch boundary, worker RSS above 6500 MiB, or 300 batches; outer hard timeout 100 s.

case_methods.torch: Ordinary torch DataLoader with the same dataset and loader arguments
case_methods.trim: Stateful loader, gc.collect plus libc malloc_trim(0) each 64 sample reads
case_methods.malloc_only: Stateful loader, only libc malloc_trim(0) each 64 sample reads
case_methods.gc_only: Stateful loader, only gc.collect each 64 sample reads
case_methods.arena2: Original stateful loader with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 inherited by child

single_item_read.mode: full transformed dataset, no batching/IPC; tracemalloc enabled
single_item_read.termination: Intentional 100-second wall-time cap, not a data error.

same_video_decode.notes: One file, torchcodec, gc.collect every 25 calls; not equivalent to shuffled full data loading.

findings: Formal training exited because Ray terminated both actors at its physical host-memory threshold after 506 updates.
The dominant memory owners were the eight data subprocesses; no formal checkpoint had been written.
Ordinary and stateful DataLoader cases both grow in CPU-only isolation.

Only malloc_trim bounds most observed RSS growth in the short diagnostic; GC alone does not. This points to retained free native-heap pages/fragmentation as a major mechanism, without attributing allocations to one dependency.
MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 reduces occupancy but still grows; it is not a verified long-run fix.
No production code was changed and formal training was not restarted. Longer data-only and checkpoint lifecycle validation remain necessary.
